Title & Venue & Year: ALIBI: Adversarial Legitimacy Injection in Binary Input against LLM Malware Analyzers | arXiv preprint | 2026
Threat Model: Black-Box (One-Query Verdict & Confidence Score; adversary submits modified Linux ELF binary to automated static triage pipeline consisting of Static Evidence Builder and Frontier LLM Malware Analyzer; budget is restricted to exactly one query; receives verdict label [benign, unknown, suspicious, malicious] and self-reported confidence score; Sec. 3, 4.4.2, 5.1, Page 3, 4, 5).
Attacker Architecture: End-to-End Single-Pass Semantic Injection Pipeline for Linux ELF via LIEF: (1) Identity Forgery populates 6 metadata attributes claiming a legitimate Linux endpoint security product identity (vendor name, product name, internal filenames, build path, build channel, telemetry endpoint); (2) Rationale Forgery crafts natural-language operational explanations tailored to a Linux security agent narrative, justifying socket connections, network scanning, and TFTP downloaders as diagnostic telemetry and administrative scans; (3) PROGBITS Section Injector adds a new non-executed PROGBITS section carrying the cover story, marked with SHF_ALLOC flag to surface in static triage evidence while strictly omitting it from PT_LOAD segments; (4) Build Metadata Overwriter updates .comment section with build identification strings matching the asserted product; leaves dynamic symbols and PLT/GOT completely untouched (Sec. 4.4.2, 4.4.3, 5.5, Page 4, 7-8).
Manager Architecture & Policy: N/A (ALIBI is a deterministic/heuristic single-pass semantic cover-story injection attack; it does not utilize reinforcement learning, agent hierarchies, or a Manager policy; Sec. 4.4.2, Page 4).
Worker Architecture & Policy: N/A (No reinforcement learning Worker agent or parameter search policy; ELF structures are updated deterministically in a single pass via the LIEF library; Sec. 4.4.2, Page 4).
State Space Representation (s_t): N/A in formal MDP terms (No iterative state transitions s_t -> s_{t+1}). Defender's static triage evidence consists of structured JSON emitted by Evidence Builder: ELF header, section header table, printable ASCII strings, dynamic symbols, and .comment metadata. Attacker observes sample's printable strings and imported socket/system calls to align Linux security agent cover story (Sec. 2.1, 4.4.2, Page 2, 4).
State Dimensions: N/A (Targets natural-language reasoning layer of frontier LLMs using variable-length JSON text, prose narratives, and ELF header metadata; no fixed d-dimensional numerical state vector is employed; Sec. 2.1, 4.4.2, Page 2, 4).
Action Selection Mechanism: Deterministic Single-Pass Rule-Based Synthesis: (1) Selects Linux endpoint security agent cover narrative adapted from EDR self-test tone; (2) Injects one new PROGBITS section holding cover story with SHF_ALLOC flag; (3) Ensures new section is NOT added to any PT_LOAD segment; (4) Overwrites .comment section with product build identification string; (5) Leaves dynamic symbol table, PLT/GOT, and executable sections completely unmodified (Sec. 4.4.2, 4.4.3, 5.5, Page 4, 7-8).
Reward Formulation: N/A for training reward (No RL optimization loop). Evaluation metrics formally defined: (1) Strict ASR = |{i | B_i = mal and A_i = ben}| / |{i | B_i = mal}| (Eq. 1, Page 6); (2) Soft ASR = |{i | B_i = mal and A_i != mal}| / |{i | B_i = mal}| (Eq. 2, Page 6); (3) Mean Delta-tier = (1/|{i | B_i = mal}|) * sum(3 - t(A_i)) with t(ben)=0, t(unk)=1, t(sus)=2, t(mal)=3 (Eq. 3, Page 6); (4) Paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for within-verdict confidence erosion (Sec. 5.2, 5.4, 5.5, Page 6, 7-8).
Integrity & Functionality Verification: Preserved by Construction (No dynamic execution sandbox required): (1) Structural Integrity: LIEF injects only one non-executed data section (PROGBITS with SHF_ALLOC) and overwrites optional .comment section; leaves dynamic symbols, relocation tables, and PLT/GOT untouched; (2) Functionality Preservation: New section is NOT mapped into any PT_LOAD program-header segment; Linux kernel loader memory mapping is completely unaltered; executable code (.text) and original execution control flow are 100% untouched (Sec. 4.4.2, 4.4.3, Page 4).
